newsitem.title: DENMARK: BADMINTON-STUER-LAURIDSEN KEEPS DANISH TITLE AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-STUER-LAURIDSEN KEEPS DANISH TITLE AT HOME.

text.p: Thomas Stuer-Lauridsen kept the Danish Open badminton title at home on Sunday with a 6-15 15-7 15-12 victory over Ong Ewe Hock of Malaysia.
The success avenged in some measure Ong's semifinal win on Saturday over Olympic champion Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen, Danish Open winner for the last three years.
Stuer-Lauridsen, 25, has won his fair share of tournaments, but in five years of trying has failed to lift the Danish Open and did not expect to do so this time.
He said: "It is my first Grand Prix win since I was injured in last year's world championships and I am at least as happy for this as I was at the time for my first Grand Prix win, in Sweden.
"The Danish Open has never been my tournament and I had no special expectations beforehand."
Stuer-Lauridsen looked outclassed in the opening game by the lightning-fast, high-leaping Ong. But he steadily gained authority and by the third game had taken control.

Danes had a good weekend. In the men's doubles final, Thomas Stavngaard and Jim Laugesen beat England's Simon Archer and Chris Hunt 17-15 10-15 15-7 while Helene Kirkegaard and Rikke Olsen took the women's title, overwhelming Julie Bradbury and Joanne Goode of England 15-6 15-2.
The host country also provided all the players in Saturdays's mixed doubles final where Michael Sogaard and Olsen routed Stavngaard and Ann Jorgensen 15-5 15-1.
China took the honours in the women's singles final on Sunday when Gong Zhichao beat Russian-born Marina Andrevskaya, now playing for Sweden 12-11 11-4.
